title: BMP uncompressed pixel rows are padded on four-byte boundaries
summary: Round width × bits per pixel up to a multiple of 32, then divide by 8 to get the row size in bytes.
applies: Windows BMP; BITMAPINFOHEADER vs. uncompressed RGB
detail: A 3-pixel wide 24-bit row has 9 color bytes with a step of 12. Pad bytes for pixels that do not belong to the next row.
boundary: Compressed BMP or other pixel formats specify otherwise; simply multiplying the width by the number of bytes cannot override line padding.
relevance: When parsing the image, the first line is correct and then gradually shifts, which is often caused by undercounting the line step size.
